questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Antenna Parameters (Radiation Pattern, Gain, Directivity, Effective Aperture, Radiation Resistance)
questions.text: Define fundamental Antenna Parameters: Radiation Pattern, Half-Power Beamwidth (HPBW), First-Null Beamwidth (FNBW), Radiation Intensity ($U$), Directivity ($D = \frac{4\pi U_{max}}{P_{rad}}$), Power Gain ($G = \eta_{cd} D$), Radiation Resistance ($R_{rad}$), Effective Aperture ($A_e = \frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi} D$), and Polarization (Linear, Circular, Elliptical).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Antenna Parameters (Radiation Pattern, Gain, Directivity, Effective Aperture, Radiation Resistance)
questions.text: Derive the radiated electric and magnetic fields ($E_\theta, H_\phi$) of a Half-Wave Dipole antenna (length $l = \lambda/2$) with sinusoidal current distribution $I(z) = I_0 \sin[k(l/2 - |z|)]$. Integrate the Poynting vector over a sphere to prove that radiation resistance is $R_{rad} = 73.13\,\Omega$ and directivity is $D = 1.64$ ($2.15\,\text{dBi}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Antenna Arrays (Linear Arrays, Broadside & End-Fire Arrays, Pattern Multiplication, Yagi-Uda)
questions.text: State the Principle of Pattern Multiplication: Total Field Pattern = (Element Pattern) $\times$ (Array Factor). Derive the Array Factor ($AF = \frac{\sin(N\psi/2)}{\sin(\psi/2)}$ where $\psi = k d \cos\theta + \beta$) for an $N$-element uniform linear array. Derive conditions for: (a) Broadside Array ($\beta = 0$), and (b) End-Fire Array ($\beta = \pm k d$). Find null directions and major lobe directions for a 4-element broadside array with spacing $d = \lambda/2$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Wire Antennas (Infinitesimal Dipole, Half-Wave Dipole, Monopole)
questions.text: Explain the construction and working of a Yagi-Uda Antenna (Driven element, Reflector, Directors). Why is the reflector approximately $5\%$ longer and directors $5\%$ shorter than the half-wave folded dipole driven element?

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Aperture & High-Frequency Antennas (Horn Antennas, Parabolic Reflectors, Microstrip Patch Antennas)
questions.text: Explain: (a) Pyramidal Horn Antenna and optimal horn design, (b) Microstrip Patch Antenna (Feeding techniques, advantages in wireless gadgets), and (c) Parabolic Reflector Antenna (Cassegrain feed, spillover, aperture efficiency, gain $G = \left(\frac{\pi D}{\lambda}\right)^2 \eta_a$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Radio Wave Propagation Mechanisms (Ground Wave, Space Wave/Tropospheric, Sky Wave/Ionospheric Propagation)
questions.text: Explain Ground (Surface) Wave Propagation at LF and MF bands. Explain Space Wave (Line-of-Sight) Propagation at VHF/UHF bands: Derive the maximum radio horizon distance $d = 4.12(\sqrt{h_t} + \sqrt{h_r})\,\text{km}$ considering earth curvature.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Radio Wave Propagation Mechanisms (Ground Wave, Space Wave/Tropospheric, Sky Wave/Ionospheric Propagation)
questions.text: Explain Sky Wave (Ionospheric) Propagation at HF bands. Describe the structure of ionospheric layers ($D, E, F_1, F_2$). Define and derive formulas for: (a) Critical Frequency ($f_c = 9\sqrt{N_{max}}$), (b) Maximum Usable Frequency ($MUF = f_c \sec i$), (c) Virtual Height, and (d) Skip Distance ($d_{skip} = 2h \sqrt{(MUF/f_c)^2 - 1}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Wire Antennas (Infinitesimal Dipole, Half-Wave Dipole, Monopole)
questions.text: Explain Quarter-Wave Monopole antenna over an infinite ground plane using the Method of Images ($R_{rad} = 36.56\,\Omega, D = 3.28$). Explain Small Loop Antennas and compare small loop fields with an infinitesimal magnetic dipole.
